data.narrative:
eGenesis, a Series C-stage biotech company founded by Luhan Yang and George Church, has raised $250M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-stage peers in Biotech & Health, with particular focus on 3 same-stage private comparables: Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B).

Two methods triangulate to a defensible range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $250M raised proxy, implying $425M valuation. Peer-median anchoring across the 3 same-sector, same-stage comparables yields $3.8B, the midpoint of a $3.1B–$10.3B range. Public-comp anchoring via sector P/S multiples (6.6x median) cannot be applied due to lack of disclosed revenue. The triangulated range spans $361M (low), $2.1B (median), to $4.4B (high) across the two applicable methods.

Key uncertainties center on stage-progression's reliance on $250M raised as a valuation proxy rather than disclosed post-money valuation, and material dispersion within the private peer set, with Colossal Biosciences trading at 2.7x the median. Revenue trajectory and clinical-stage risk profile drive valuation variance within peers and merit further diligence.
